source: Evaluated at runtime by dust_extinction 1.7 (parameter_averages.CCM89), the astropy-affiliated implementation of Cardelli+1989; this file is the audited copy of that same fit, transcribed from two independent open implementations that agree digit-for-digit -- dust_extinction 1.7 (re-read from the installed source: NIR L124-127, optical np.polyval L130-137, NUV L139-146, far-NUV L148-151, Rv_range/x_range L87-88) and extinction 0.4.8 (_extinction.pyx L38-97). It supplies the domain this build enforces, the provenance every result reports and the pins the suite checks the package against; it is NOT re-read from the paper's pages, which are not retrievable here.
ordering_note: dust_extinction passes the optical coefficients to np.polyval in DESCENDING powers; the lists below are ASCENDING (c[k] multiplies y**k), i.e. reversed. That reversal is the transcription trap recorded under transcription_warning.

nir.form: a = a_coef * x**exponent, b = b_coef * x**exponent

optical.form: polynomials in y = x - y_offset, coefficients in ascending order

uv.form: a = constant + linear*x + feature/((x-x0)**2 + gamma_sq); b likewise

far_uv.form: added to the uv branch for x >= x_from; polynomial in y = x - y_offset, ascending

normalisation: A(V)/A(V) = 1 at x = 1/0.54945 micron^-1 for every R_V: the optical b polynomial has zero constant term and the a polynomial equals 1 there.

structural_oracles.how_to_read: These are checkable without the paper's tables, because each is a property the fit is *defined* to have, or a discontinuity only a transcription error creates. tests/test_extinction.py asserts these; it does not assert a tabulated a(x) or b(x).
structural_oracles.a_v_normalisation: a(x_V) + b(x_V)/R_V = 1 for R_V = 3.1 (and any R_V) -- an independent check, since it is the definition of A(V), and it fails at once if the polynomial coefficient order is inverted
structural_oracles.uv_bump: A(2175 A)/A(V) > A(2700 A)/A(V) and > A(1500 A)/A(V): the 2175 A feature is the (x - 4.67)^-2 term, so it IS applied, unlike in a smooth-only parameterisation
structural_oracles.branch_steps: the piecewise fit is continuous to ~3e-4 mag at x = 1.1 and ~2e-4 at x = 3.3; a mis-copied coefficient shows up as a step of order 0.1 mag or more. The far-NUV addition joins at x = 5.9 with zero discontinuity by construction, since its polynomial has no constant or linear term. The fourth join is x = 8.0 -- the domain's blue edge, 1250 A -- and it leaves 1.8191e-04 mag between the sides: 3.3368593254 on the <=8 branch, 3.3366774201 on the >8 branch (the latter is the segment this file does not transcribe, see excluded.fuv_x_gt_8). dust_extinction 1.7 and this build both give x = 8.0 to the <=8 side and agree there exactly; extinction 0.4.8 gives it to the >8 side, so a reader comparing the 1250 A endpoint against that package sees 1.8191e-04 mag (0.182 mmag), which is branch ownership, not a transcription error.
structural_oracles.optical_monotonic: A(x)/A(V) decreases monotonically with wavelength across the optical branch, which is what the V normalisation plus a positive R_V-dependent b term require

self_checks.how_to_read: Regression PINS, not oracles: these are the numbers this transcription produces, recorded so that editing a coefficient cannot pass silently. A wrong digit in the paper's own table would be reproduced faithfully here; only a re-read of ApJ 345, 245 could catch that. Each extremum names its own location, because the maximum over the domain is NOT the 2175 A bump: it sits at the blue edge (x = 8.0) and is 0.151758 mag above A_2175A_over_A_V, i.e. about 15 % in flux.

transcription_warning: The Horner rendering of the optical b polynomial in one secondary write-up places its constant term last, which reads as b(x_V) = 1.41338 and gives A(B)/A(V) = 1.71 instead of 1.32. The b polynomial has NO constant term; 1.41338 multiplies y. This file records the ordering that reproduces A(V)/A(V) = 1.

excluded.fuv_x_gt_8: CCM89's 8 < x <= 10 and x <= 11 segments exist in the implementations above but reach 1000 A, bluer than any band this project builds; requests beyond x = 8 raise rather than extrapolate. 1250-33333 A is the parameterisation's own inverse-micron domain (x = 8.0 down to x = 0.3), not the paper's claim: CCM89's abstract quotes a 0.125-3.5 micron window, whose red end lies beyond x = 0.3, and the 3.3-3.5 micron tail is therefore refused here as out of domain even though the abstract includes it.
excluded.24_knot_spline_table: Referred to in secondary descriptions as an interpolated a(x), b(x) table; zero of the 24 knots could be read from any retrievable source, so none is transcribed. The analytic branches above are complete over x_range.
excluded.u_equals_lambda_minus_0p5359_nir_form: A functional form attributed to CCM89 in some write-ups that neither implementation above uses; unverified, so not used.
excluded.natural_cubic_spline_uv_method: Belongs to Fitzpatrick & Sneden 1999, not CCM89. Attributing it to CCM89 is a law mix-up.
excluded.upsilon_4p59_gamma_90_bump: A Draine-style bump parameterisation with those constants could not be confirmed in any open source and is not CCM89's own.
excluded.ccm_1990_erratum: An erratum at ApJ 356, 319 is sometimes cited; Crossref carries no correction link to the 1989 record and no such paper was found, so nothing is assumed to have changed.
